title: Major proved; pagan confession — Cap. 8 close
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Ye major in two ways is proved. First, because an independent being or one from itself existing by ye force belonging toward its essence or nature exists, plus therefore existence unto it as necessarily as essence belongs. Second, because an independent being neither once not to have been could, nor hereafter not be. Therefore absolutely necessary it is. FOURTH, also by ye confession belonging toward Gentile philosophers. For Orpheus ye necessity belonging toward all things spoke of — that is, a substance which through itself necessarily is, plus on which all ye rest depend, but itself on none. Aristotle God a necessary, perpetual being calls. Apuleius: necessity itself nothing other than God to be called I would judge. Avicenna: That holy thing ye necessary being which from itself is, but not ye remaining beings, even if from another necessity belonging toward existing they have.
pass_b_english: The major is proved in two ways. First, because an independent being or one existing from itself exists by the force of its essence or nature, and therefore existence belongs to it as necessarily as essence. Second, because an independent being neither could once not have been, nor hereafter not be. Therefore it is absolutely necessary.

FOURTH, also by the confession of Gentile philosophers. For Orpheus spoke of the necessity of all things — that is, a substance which is necessarily through itself, and on which all the rest depend, but itself on none. Aristotle calls God a necessary, perpetual being. Apuleius: I would judge necessity itself to be called nothing other than God. Avicenna: That holy thing is the necessary being which is from itself, but not the remaining beings, even if they have necessity of existing from another.
source_text: Major duobus modis probatur. Primo, quia ens independens vel exsistens a seipso, exsistit vi essentiae sive naturae suae, ac proinde illi exsistentia tam necessario competit, quam essentia. Secundo, quia ens independens, nec potuit aliquando non fuisse, nec posthac non esse. Ergo est absolute necessarium. QUARTO, Confessione etiam gentilium philosophorum. Orpheus enim dixit rerum omnium necessitatem, hoc est, substantiam, quae sit necessario per seipsam, & a qua caetera omnia dependeant, ipsa vero a nullo. Aristoteles: Deum dicit, ens necessarium, perpetuum. Apulejus: necessitatem ipsam nihil aliud, quam Deum, dici censuerim. Avicenna: Illud sanctum esse ens necessarium, quod ex se est, non vero entia reliqua, etiamsi ab alio habeant necessitatem exsistendi.
